agree.reason: The 3 a.m. solo shift and the nine early mastitis cases make a sympathetic, believable case, but a committee member reading quickly gets few hard numbers or commitments to set Tomás apart from 150 applicants.

honest.reason: The letter mostly sticks to the facts, but 'seriously ill', 'Nobody required him' and 'enrolled... on his own' go beyond the brief, and putting 'only two shifts' right next to the five-week absence plays down that gap.

works_the_facts.reason: Nothing is calculated: the letter never turns two missed shifts into roughly 2 of about 780 shifts, and it doesn't use the vet's $8,000 savings figure to show what the early catches were worth.

right_comparison.reason: It doesn't show what sets Tomás apart from a typical applicant, or how his three-year record compares with ordinary farm workers beyond the general claim that 'that kind of reliability is rare'.

qualification.reason: A letter of recommendation doesn't need hedged conditions, and this one has none.

objections.reason: The night class partly answers the worry about his written English, but the letter leaves the five-week absence open to doubt when it could have said he arranged his cousin to cover his shifts and came back on the day he promised, and it never mentions the part-time weekend job offer that would support him finishing the program.

fit.reason: It's a one-page letter from the farm manager as the brief asked, but placeholders remain for the name, farm and phone number, all of which the user had available.
